ARABIC LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which Arabic sentence means "What is your name? (to a girl)" (1 mark)
   A. أَنَا تِلْمِيذٌ
   B. اسْمِي أَحْمَدُ
   C. أَنَا تِلْمِيذَةٌ
   D. مَا اسْمُكِ؟

2. How is the Arabic word مَا اسْمُكَ؟ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. maa ismuka?
   B. ahlan wa sahlan
   C. as-salaamu ʿalaykum
   D. shukran

3. What does the Arabic sentence هَذِهِ أُمِّي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I have a brother and a sister.
   B. My father works.
   C. This is my father.
   D. This is my mother.

4. How is the Arabic word أُسْرَةٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. khaal
   B. bint
   C. ukht
   D. usra

5. How is the Arabic word كِتَابٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. misbaah
   B. kitaab
   C. naafidha
   D. qalam

6. What does the Arabic sentence أَيْنَ الْكِتَابُ؟ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The lamp is above the table.
   B. The cat is under the bed.
   C. The book is on the table.
   D. Where is the book?

7. Which Arabic instruction means 'sit down'? (1 mark)
   A. qif
   B. ukhruj
   C. ijlis
   D. iqraʾ

8. Which Arabic sentence means "I go to school on Monday." (1 mark)
   A. أَلْعَبُ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ
   B. الْيَوْمُ يَوْمُ الْخَمِيسِ
   C. أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ
   D. فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ سَبْعَةُ أَيَّامٍ

9. What does the Arabic word مَدْرَسَةٌ (madrasa) mean? (1 mark)
   A. yesterday
   B. Monday
   C. day
   D. school

10. What does the Arabic word لَا (laa) mean? (1 mark)
   A. song
   B. your turn
   C. no
   D. cake

11. What does the Arabic sentence هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَفْلَةٌ؟ mean? (1 mark)
   A. Do you have a party? (to a boy)
   B. Happy birthday.
   C. May you be well every year.
   D. Blessed festival (Happy Eid).

12. What does the Arabic word بَطَاطِسُ (bataatis) mean? (1 mark)
   A. potatoes
   B. tomatoes
   C. maize
   D. eggs

13. What does the Arabic word بَيْضٌ (bayd) mean? (1 mark)
   A. meat
   B. eggs
   C. chicken
   D. carrots

14. What does the Arabic sentence هَذَا رَأْسِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I see with my eye.
   B. I smell with my nose.
   C. I hear with my ear.
   D. This is my head.

15. Which body part is used for the action 'aktubu' (I write)? (1 mark)
   A. fam, the mouth
   B. yad, the hand
   C. udhun, the ear
   D. anf, the nose

16. What does the Arabic word ظَهْرٌ (dhahr) mean? (1 mark)
   A. ear
   B. back
   C. leg
   D. nose

17. Which Arabic sentence means "The water is clean." (1 mark)
   A. الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ
   B. الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ
   C. الْجَوُّ مُمْطِرٌ
   D. الْمَاءُ نَظِيفٌ

18. Which is a good way to take care of the environment? (1 mark)
   A. Cut trees without planting new ones
   B. Throw rubbish in the river
   C. Burn plastic in the open
   D. Plant trees and keep the surroundings clean

19. What are the three parts of a short speech? (1 mark)
   A. Opening, middle and closing
   B. Song, dance and drum
   C. Title, picture and page
   D. Question, answer and test

20. Which phrase do you use to thank the audience? (1 mark)
   A. maa ismuka?
   B. shukran li-istimaaʿikum
   C. kayfa haaluka?
   D. as-salaamu ʿalaykum

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain the difference between a direct question and an inferential question. Give one example of each about a text on breakfast. (4 marks) (4 marks)

22. Write five parts of the body in Arabic (English letters are fine) with their meanings. (5 marks) (5 marks)

23. Give three ways in which a family can reduce food wastage at home. (3 marks) (3 marks)

24. Translate into English: man haadhaa? (2 marks)

25. Give two reasons why we should take care of household items. (2 marks) (2 marks)

26. Write in Arabic sounds and translate: 'Today is Thursday.' (2 marks) (2 marks)

27. Translate into English: kayfa haaluki? (2 marks)

28. Translate into English: uhibbu l-ʿasiira (2 marks)

29. Write in Arabic sounds and translate: 'The weather is cold.' (2 marks) (2 marks)

30. Translate into English: jaddatii tuhibbunii (2 marks)

31. Translate into English: fii baytii matbakh (2 marks)

32. Write in Arabic sounds and translate: 'I eat bread and I drink milk.' (2 marks) (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #19 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — مَا اسْمُكِ؟
   مَا اسْمُكِ؟ (maa ismuki?) means: What is your name? (to a girl)

2. A — maa ismuka?
   مَا اسْمُكَ؟ is read maa ismuka? and means What is your name? (to a boy).

3. D — This is my mother.
   هَذِهِ أُمِّي (haadhihi ummii) means: This is my mother.

4. D — usra
   أُسْرَةٌ is read usra and means family.

5. B — kitaab
   كِتَابٌ is read kitaab and means book.

6. D — Where is the book?
   أَيْنَ الْكِتَابُ؟ (ayna l-kitaab?) means: Where is the book?

7. C — ijlis
   ijlis means sit down. qif means stand up.

8. C — أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ
   أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ (adhhabu ilaa l-madrasa yawma l-ithnayn) means: I go to school on Monday.

9. D — school
   مَدْرَسَةٌ (madrasa) means school.

10. C — no
   لَا (laa) means no.

11. A — Do you have a party? (to a boy)
   هَلْ عِنْدَكَ حَفْلَةٌ؟ (hal ʿindaka hafla?) means: Do you have a party? (to a boy)

12. A — potatoes
   بَطَاطِسُ (bataatis) means potatoes.

13. B — eggs
   بَيْضٌ (bayd) means eggs.

14. D — This is my head.
   هَذَا رَأْسِي (haadhaa raʾsii) means: This is my head.

15. B — yad, the hand
   We write with the hand (yad).

16. B — back
   ظَهْرٌ (dhahr) means back.

17. D — الْمَاءُ نَظِيفٌ
   الْمَاءُ نَظِيفٌ (al-maa'u nadhiif) means: The water is clean.

18. D — Plant trees and keep the surroundings clean
   Planting trees and keeping the area clean protect the environment.

19. A — Opening, middle and closing
   A speech opens by greeting, gives the main information and closes by thanking.

20. B — shukran li-istimaaʿikum
   shukran li-istimaaʿikum means 'thank you for listening'.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: A direct question has its answer in the text, for example 'What does she drink?' An inferential question needs clues, for example 'Is it morning?'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each definition and 1 mark for each suitable example.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: For example raʾs (head), wajh (face), shaʿr (hair), ʿayn (eye), udhun (ear).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with its meaning.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Cook only what is needed; store leftovers and eat them later; share extra food; use peels for compost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible way.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: Who is this? (a boy or man)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: They last longer and save money, and keeping them in the right place keeps us safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: al-yawmu yawmu l-khamiis. Today is Thursday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the Arabic sounds and 1 mark for the translation.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: How are you? (to a girl)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: I like juice.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: al-jawwu baarid. The weather is cold.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the Arabic sounds and 1 mark for the translation.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: My grandmother loves me.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

31. (2 marks)
   Answer: In my house there is a kitchen.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: aakulu l-khubza wa ashrabu l-haliiba. I eat bread and I drink milk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the Arabic sounds and 1 mark for the translation.
